blocks.text: Published by Éditions Odyssée , “Aquapelago, atlas d’une ville invisible” offers an exploration of the territory formed by Venice and its lagoon. Turning away from picturesque or documentary representations, photographer Marco Berti Palazzi delivers a singular portrait, a visual meditation in which emptiness and fullness, water and land, silence and presence answer one another.

His gaze lingers on the shifting borders between land and water, building a narrative based on subtle chromatic variations and rigorous composition. The photographs reveal a territory in perpetual transformation, where natural spaces and architecture bear witness to a landscape shaped over the centuries by the interactions between environments and human activities. They draw a geography of the lagoon that reveals less a city than a way of inhabiting and perceiving it.
The photographic series is accompanied by an essay by Italian researcher Laura Cipriani, devoted to the history, transformations and contemporary challenges of this singular territory.

Born of a collaboration between two institutions from the world of images, the Prix Escourbiac – Fondation des Treilles supports the creation of photobooks by exploring the many facets of the Mediterranean basin. The 2026 laureate, Marco Berti Palazzi, is an Italian photographer living in Brussels.
“Every time I describe a city I am saying something about Venice.” Italo Calvino, Invisible Cities

“For as long as anyone can remember, the lagoon and its islands have oscillated between these two poles: permanence and metamorphosis. […] The debates and projects of tomorrow necessarily begin with an account of the present, of the conflict between man and nature, between past and future, between the desire for permanence and the need for metamorphosis.” Laura Cipriani

Marco Berti Palazzi Marco Berti Palazzi explores urban and extra-urban territories in the manner of a “sidewalk botanist.” Favoring wandering and a slow way of looking, he photographs “anthropized” and vernacular landscapes made up of places, objects and simple, ordinary architecture – silent, discreet traces of the human condition. He trained over the years at the Académie des Arts de Woluwe-Saint-Pierre in Brussels, and through workshops, notably with Klavdij Sluban and Claudine Doury. He self-published the book “Un pays froid où le soleil est chaud,” a visual account of his multi-year stay in Morocco.

The Fondation des Treilles The Fondation des Treilles, created by Anne Gruner Schlumberger, is dedicated in particular to nurturing dialogue between the sciences and the arts in order to advance creation and research. It hosts researchers and creators at its estate, the Domaine des Treilles (Var). www.les-treilles.com

Escourbiac l’imprimeur Escourbiac l’imprimeur is a family-run printing house located in the South-West of France and managed by brothers Philippe and Alain Escourbiac. A specialist in photobooks, it is recognized for the quality of its work. Escourbiac l’imprimeur is distinctive in bringing together on a single site, in the heart of the Tarn, all the skills of photobook production, from image processing to binding. www.escourbiac.com
